transcript.text: fridge part freezin stuff, lettuce + yoghurts frozen solid at the back. hotpoint ff. any ideas pls

This usually happens for one of three reasons: something is touching the cold back wall (which freezes items instantly), the thermostat is set too low or a 'fast freeze' mode is active, or there is an internal airflow issue like a blocked drain causing frost build-up. Please check that your temperature dial isn't on its coldest setting and ensure no food is pressed against the rear panel or vents.
dial is on max, kids prob moved it. food is rammed against the back vents too after big shop. what should i do?

The main culprit is likely the dial being on 'Max', which makes the fridge run much colder than necessary. Combined with food blocking the vents at the back, cold air isn't circulating properly and freezes items instantly. Here is what to do:
1. Move all the food away from the back wall so there is space for air to flow.
2. Turn the temperature dial down to a mid-range setting (usually around 3 or 4).
3. Leave it like that for 24 hours. If the frozen items thaw and stay fresh after this, you are good to go. If they freeze up again despite being moved away from the wall and with the dial lowered, we will need to check if there is an internal defrost fault.
did that, been 2 days. better now but one yoghurt still froze right at the very back. is that normal?

It is not normal for food to freeze solid after you have corrected the settings and spacing. Since it has been two days and one item at the very back is still freezing, this usually points to a blocked defrost drain or a minor fault with the automatic defrost system (where ice builds up behind the back panel and blocks airflow). Please do a full manual defrost: switch the fridge off at the wall, move the food into cool bags, and leave the doors open for 24 hours until all ice has melted. Once it is dry, check the small drain hole at the bottom of the back interior wall—pour a little warm water in to see if it drains away freely or if it pools up.

candidates: Food touching the cold back wall or vents (high)
Thermostat setting too cold or fast-freeze mode on (medium)
Defrost system fault (blocked drain or failed heater) (low)
